units.name: command-model
units.role: Defines the Command tree and drives argument parsing, subcommand dispatch, and help/usage output.
units.description: This is the heart of Cobra: the Command type that a CLI author assembles into a tree of commands and subcommands, plus the machinery that turns process arguments into a decision about which command to run, parses that command's flags, and prints its help, usage, error, and version text. It also contains a small Windows-only guard that detects a CLI launched by double-clicking it in Explorer (instead of from a terminal) and shows an explanatory message instead of a console window that immediately closes.

entrypoints.name: Command
entrypoints.plain: The struct a CLI is built from: one node in the command tree, holding its flags, subcommands, Run function, and help/usage settings.

entrypoints.name: Execute
entrypoints.plain: The call most Cobra programs make from main(): parses process arguments and runs the resolved (sub)command.

entrypoints.name: ExecuteContext
entrypoints.plain: Same as Execute, but lets the caller supply a context.Context that flows through to Run.

entrypoints.name: ExecuteC
entrypoints.plain: Does the actual work behind Execute and also reports back which command was run; almost all execution logic lives here.

entrypoints.name: Find
entrypoints.plain: Walks the command tree to figure out which (sub)command a given slice of CLI args refers to.

entrypoints.name: AddCommand
entrypoints.plain: Registers one or more subcommands under this command, building the command tree.

entrypoints.name: Commands
entrypoints.plain: Returns this command's direct subcommands.

entrypoints.name: Root
entrypoints.plain: Walks up to and returns the top-level command of the tree.

entrypoints.name: Name
entrypoints.plain: Returns the command's own name (the first word of its Use string).

entrypoints.name: CommandPath
entrypoints.plain: Returns the full space-separated path from the root command down to this one, e.g. "git remote add".

entrypoints.name: IsAvailableCommand
entrypoints.plain: Reports whether this command should be shown in help listings (not hidden, not deprecated, runnable or has visible children).

entrypoints.name: Flags
entrypoints.plain: Returns this command's full set of flags (local plus persistent), creating it on first use.

entrypoints.name: PersistentFlags
entrypoints.plain: Returns the flags that are also inherited by every subcommand.

entrypoints.name: Help
entrypoints.plain: Prints this command's help text using its (or an inherited) help function.

entrypoints.name: ValidateArgs
entrypoints.plain: Runs the command's positional-argument validator (its Args field) against the leftover, non-flag arguments.

entrypoints.name: SetArgs
entrypoints.plain: Overrides the argument slice Execute parses; without this it defaults to os.Args[1:].

effects.description: Reads process arguments from os.Args[1:] when SetArgs has not been called (command.go:1105-1106).

Writes help/usage/error/version text to stdout or stderr (or a caller-supplied io.Writer), defaulting to os.Stdout/os.Stderr, via OutOrStdout/OutOrStderr/ErrOrStderr and InOrStdin defaulting to os.Stdin (command.go:393-409).

A generic filesystem-effect scanner flags the substring "fs." in fs.Lookup(...)/fs.ShorthandLookup(...) (command.go:655,667), where `fs` is a local *pflag.FlagSet variable; this is flag lookup, not disk I/O.
The Windows mousetrap guard calls os.Exit(1) to terminate the process before Run executes, when the binary was double-clicked from Explorer (command_win.go:39).
The Windows mousetrap guard sleeps for MousetrapDisplayDuration before continuing (command_win.go:33-34).
The Windows mousetrap guard blocks on fmt.Scanln() to wait for a keypress from stdin when MousetrapDisplayDuration is 0 (command_win.go:37).

units.name: positional-args
units.role: Ready-made and combinable validators for a command's leftover (non-flag) positional arguments.
units.description: A small library of functions that check the positional arguments left over after flag parsing: exactly N, at least N, at most N, a range, no duplicates, only values from an allow-list, or no arguments at all. They plug into a Command's Args field and can be combined with MatchAll. This file has no side effects of its own; it only inspects the argument slice and the owning Command's configuration.

entrypoints.name: PositionalArgs
entrypoints.plain: The function signature every positional-argument validator implements; assigned to Command.Args.

entrypoints.name: legacyArgs
entrypoints.plain: Cobra's default validator when Args is left unset: root commands with subcommands reject unknown subcommand names, everything else accepts anything.

entrypoints.name: NoArgs
entrypoints.plain: Rejects the command if it was given any positional arguments.

entrypoints.name: OnlyValidArgs
entrypoints.plain: Rejects any positional argument not listed in the command's ValidArgs.

entrypoints.name: NoDuplicateArgs
entrypoints.plain: Rejects the command if the same positional argument value appears twice.

entrypoints.name: ArbitraryArgs
entrypoints.plain: Accepts any positional arguments; never errors.

entrypoints.name: RangeArgs
entrypoints.signature: func RangeArgs(min int, max int) PositionalArgs

entrypoints.name: MatchAll
entrypoints.plain: Combines several PositionalArgs validators so all of them must pass.

entrypoints.name: ExactValidArgs
entrypoints.plain: Deprecated shortcut for MatchAll(ExactArgs(n), OnlyValidArgs).

units.name: template-runtime
units.role: Global, package-wide configuration knobs, help/usage template plumbing, and small text/comparison utilities.
units.description: Cross-cutting support code shared by the rest of the library: the registry of custom template functions usable inside help and usage templates, the OnInitialize/OnFinalize hook lists that run around every Execute call, package-level toggles like prefix matching and command sorting, a levenshtein-distance helper used to suggest the closest command name on a typo, and CheckErr, a small helper for printing an error and exiting the process. Nothing here refers to the Command type; other units call into it, not the reverse.

entrypoints.name: AddTemplateFunc
entrypoints.plain: Registers one named function that Usage/Help templates can call.

entrypoints.name: AddTemplateFuncs
entrypoints.plain: Registers several template functions at once.

entrypoints.name: OnInitialize
entrypoints.plain: Queues functions to run at the start of every command's Execute.

entrypoints.name: OnFinalize
entrypoints.plain: Queues functions to run at the end of every command's Execute.

entrypoints.name: Gt
entrypoints.plain: Template helper: is the first value greater than the second (lengths for collections, else numeric/string compare).

entrypoints.name: Eq
entrypoints.plain: Template helper: are two int or string values equal.

entrypoints.name: CheckErr
entrypoints.plain: Prints "Error: <msg>" to stderr and exits the process with status 1, if msg is non-nil.

entrypoints.name: WriteStringAndCheck
entrypoints.plain: Writes a string to a writer and calls CheckErr on any error.

entrypoints.name: tmpl
entrypoints.plain: Compiles a help/usage template string, bound to the current template function registry, into a reusable renderer.

entrypoints.name: ld
entrypoints.plain: Levenshtein edit distance between two strings, used to suggest a likely-intended command name after a typo.

entrypoints.name: rpad
entrypoints.plain: Right-pads a string with spaces to a given width, for aligning help-listing columns.

effects.description: CheckErr writes "Error: <msg>" to os.Stderr and calls os.Exit(1), terminating the process, whenever it is given a non-nil error (cobra.go:235-240).

units.name: flag-groups
units.role: Declarative constraints across a command's flags: required-together, one-of-required, mutually exclusive.
units.description: Lets a command declare relationships between several of its flags, such as "if any of these is set, all of them must be" or "exactly one of these must be set", by attaching annotations to the flags via pflag. ValidateFlagGroups checks those annotations against which flags were actually set and is run automatically as part of Execute. It builds directly on the pflag.FlagSet exposed by a Command's Flags()/PersistentFlags().

entrypoints.name: ValidateFlagGroups
entrypoints.plain: Checks all of a command's declared flag-group constraints against which flags were actually set, returning an error on violation. Called automatically during Execute.

effects.description: A generic filesystem-effect scanner flags the substring "fs." in fs.Lookup(...) (flag_groups.go:113), where `fs` is a local *pflag.FlagSet variable; this is flag lookup, not disk I/O.

units.name: shell-completions
units.role: Dynamic tab-completion protocol plus static completion-script generation for bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell.
units.description: Everything related to shell tab-completion: the __complete/__completeNoDesc runtime protocol and its ShellCompDirective/CompletionFunc types, per-flag completion registration, ActiveHelp hint messages, flag annotations that mark a flag as filename/dirname/custom completion, and the generators that emit a static completion script for bash (legacy and dynamic v2), zsh, fish, or PowerShell. These eight files are treated as one unit because they share unexported constants and helper functions across file boundaries rather than exposing a clean internal interface between the completion protocol and each shell's script generator.

entrypoints.name: ShellCompDirective
entrypoints.plain: A bitmask a completion function returns alongside its suggestions, e.g. "no file completion" or "no space after".

entrypoints.name: CompletionFunc
entrypoints.plain: The function signature a flag or command registers to supply its own dynamic completions.

entrypoints.name: NoFileCompletions
entrypoints.plain: A CompletionFunc that suggests nothing and disables the shell's default filename completion.

entrypoints.name: FixedCompletions
entrypoints.plain: Builds a CompletionFunc that always returns the same fixed list of choices.

entrypoints.name: RegisterFlagCompletionFunc
entrypoints.signature: func (c *Command) RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(flagName string, f CompletionFunc) error
entrypoints.plain: Attaches a custom dynamic-completion function to one of a command's flags.

entrypoints.name: InitDefaultCompletionCmd
entrypoints.plain: Adds the built-in "completion" and hidden "__complete"/"__completeNoDesc" subcommands that implement the shell-completion protocol.

entrypoints.name: CompDebug
entrypoints.plain: Writes a completion-debug message, optionally to stderr and always to the file named by BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE if set.

entrypoints.name: AppendActiveHelp
entrypoints.plain: Appends an ActiveHelp hint string to a list of completions, using the marker convention shells recognize.

entrypoints.name: GetActiveHelpConfig
entrypoints.plain: Reads the per-command and global environment variables that let a user disable or configure ActiveHelp hints.

entrypoints.name: MarkFlagFilename
entrypoints.plain: Limits completions for a flag to files with the given extensions.

entrypoints.name: MarkFlagDirname
entrypoints.plain: Limits completions for a flag to directory names.

entrypoints.name: GenBashCompletion
entrypoints.plain: Writes a legacy (v1) bash completion script for this command tree to a writer.

entrypoints.name: GenBashCompletionV2
entrypoints.plain: Writes a dynamic (v2) bash completion script, which calls back into the program itself, to a writer.

effects.description: The GenXxxCompletionFile methods write a completion script to disk via os.Create (bash_completions.go:702, bash_completionsV2.go:471, zsh_completions.go:71, fish_completions.go:285, powershell_completions.go:321).
CompDebug opens (and appends to) the file named by the BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE environment variable via os.OpenFile, when that variable is set (completions.go:962).

Reads BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE to enable completion debug logging, and per-command/global env vars (via configEnvVar/activeHelpEnvVar) to configure descriptions and ActiveHelp (completions.go:960,1019,1021; active_help.go:48,50).
CompDebug/CompError write completion debug/error text to stderr in addition to (or instead of) the debug file (completions.go:955-991).

units.name: doc-generators
units.role: Renders a Cobra command tree into Markdown, man pages, reStructuredText, or YAML documentation files.
units.description: A separate Go package (doc) built on top of the root Cobra package: given a root Command, it walks the whole command tree and writes one documentation file per command, in the caller's choice of Markdown, Unix man page (troff), reStructuredText, or YAML, either to a supplied writer or as a tree of files in a directory. It is purely a consumer of the command-model unit's public API (command names, flags, help text, subcommands) and performs no domain logic of its own beyond formatting.

entrypoints.name: GenMarkdownTree
entrypoints.plain: Writes one Markdown file per command in the tree, into a directory.

entrypoints.name: GenMan
entrypoints.signature: func GenMan(cmd *cobra.Command, header *GenManHeader, w io.Writer) error

entrypoints.name: GenManTree
entrypoints.plain: Writes one Unix man page per command in the tree, into a directory.

entrypoints.name: GenReSTTree
entrypoints.plain: Writes one reStructuredText file per command in the tree, into a directory.

entrypoints.name: GenYamlTree
entrypoints.plain: Writes one YAML file per command in the tree, into a directory.

effects.description: GenMarkdownTree/GenManTree/GenReSTTree/GenYamlTree each create one output file per command via os.Create (doc/md_docs.go:145, doc/man_docs.go:72, doc/rest_docs.go:157, doc/yaml_docs.go:72).
GenMan reads SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH to produce a reproducible build date on the man page instead of the current date (doc/man_docs.go:127).
GenMan/GenMarkdown/GenReST stamp the generated document with time.Now() when no reproducible date override is set (doc/man_docs.go:126, doc/md_docs.go:113, doc/rest_docs.go:126).
